question: In covering a distance of 56 km, Pranshu takes 3 hours more than Chandu. If Pranshu doubles his speed, he would take 4 hours less than Chandu. Pranshu's speed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Pranshu's speed ratio (Original : New) = 1 : 2 ⇒ Time ratio = 2 : 1

Difference in time ratio = 2 − 1 = 1 unit

Total time gap = 3 hours (more) + 4 hours (less) = 7 hours

⇒ 1 unit = 7 hours ⇒ Original time (2 units) = 14 hours

Pranshu's original speed = 56 ÷ 14 = 4 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 4 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 56 km

Let Pranshu's original time be tP and Chandu's time be tC.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 
• 
 
 
 Distance = 56 km

 
• 
 

 Original: Speed = P, Time = t⊂C&endsub; + 3

 
• 
 

 Doubled: Speed = 2P, Time = t⊂C&endsub; − 4
 
 Difference in Time = 7 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Case 1: Pranshu takes 3 hours more than Chandu ⇒ tP − tC = 3 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Case 2: When Pranshu doubles his speed, his time becomes half, i.e., tP ÷ 2

⇒ Now, he takes 4 hours less than Chandu ⇒ tC − (tP ÷ 2) = 4 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ (tP − tC) + (tC − tP ÷ 2) = 3 + 4

⇒ tP − (tP ÷ 2) = 7

⇒ tP ÷ 2 = 7

⇒ tP = 14 hours

⇒ Pranshu's speed = Total Distance ÷ tP

⇒ Speed = 56 ÷ 14 = 4 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 4 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality of Speed and Time

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1 ÷ T). If the ratio of speeds is a : b, the corresponding ratio of times taken will be b : a.

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed

If two equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, the Average Speed is given by (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).
